focusPost.content: It’s ironic how we blame China for our own manufacturing inferiority. As the article states, “Chinese manufacturers are adept at mass-producing electric vehicles.” The problem is ours, not theirs. It’s simply a reflection of our money obsessed culture that prizes profits above all else. Above health. More than life itself. Our laws and court actions have repeatedly reaffirmed a company’s highest responsibility is to “maximize shareholder value.” Which means make as much money as possible, as quickly as possible, any way possible. The fastest way a manufacturing company can boost its profits is to cut costs. Mortgage the future for the sake of a few more dollars today. In the process we’ve ceded manufacturing to China and other countries who can make EVs, and most other manufactured goods, better than we can. Over the past few decades we’ve rationalized becoming a “service” economy or an “information” economy. Funny how making things is still important. Cars, iPhones, solar panels, wind turbines, batteries, all of which we rely on China to make for us. By resorting to tariffs we’re only making consumers pay more for things that we can’t manufacture as well or as inexpensively as others can. If we want to blame someone for our loss of manufacturing prowess, we have only to look in the mirror.

Cars, iPhones, solar panels, wind turbines, batteries, all of which we rely on China to make for us.
